property_summary: After calling setOwner with a new address, the reference updates owner to that address while the bug keeps the original owner, so a subsequent call to owner() returns different values.
After calling setOwner(alice) as alice, the reference contract sets owner to alice, while the mutant sets owner to address(0).

After calling setOwner(alice) as alice (the owner), the reference sets owner to alice while the mutant sets owner to address(0); an assertion that owner == alice passes on reference but fails on mutant.
After owner calls setOwner(0x1234...), the reference sets owner to the argument while the bug sets it to 0x0001; reading owner() returns different addresses.
After calling setOwner(alice) as the original owner, the reference contract has owner == alice while the buggy one has owner == address(0).
After a non-owner calls setOwner(newOwner), the reference contract reverts (owner unchanged) while the buggy contract changes owner to newOwner.
Calling setOwner(alice) as alice should update the owner to alice; the buggy version reverts due to require(false), leaving owner unchanged.
Calling setOwner(alice) as alice in the reference sets owner to alice; in the buggy version the tx reverts due to require(false) and owner stays as the deployer (the test contract).
After deployer calls setOwner(alice) as alice, the reference sets owner to alice; the buggy version reverts and owner remains as the test contract (deployer).
After the deployer calls setOwner(alice) as alice, the reference contract sets owner to alice, whereas the buggy contract reverts and owner remains the original deployer.
Calling setOwner(alice) as alice in the reference contract updates owner to alice; in the buggy contract the call reverts and owner remains the test contract.

After a call to setOwner(address) by the original owner, the reference contract updates owner to the new address, while the buggy contract reverts because its require condition always fails, causing divergence.

After calling setOwner(address) from the original owner, the reference updates owner to the argument, but the buggy version's require fails because it always compares msg.sender to address(0), so owner remains unchanged.
After calling setOwner(alice) as owner, the correct contract returns true, while the buggy one returns false.

After calling setOwner(address) as the original owner, the owner becomes the argument address in the reference but msg.sender in the buggy version, so when called by address(0x123) with argument address(0x456), the reference sets owner to 0x456 and the buggy set to 0x123.

After calling setOwner with a new address, the reference updates owner to that address, while the buggy version keeps owner unchanged. The test sets owner to address(0x123) via setOwner and asserts that owner returns address(0x123).
